The graph of $y=f(x),$ shown above, consists of four line segments. Find the value of ${\int }_{-3}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x.$
questions.worked_solution:
The graph consists of four parts: the line segment for $x\in [-3,-2),$ the line segment for $x\in [-2,-1),$ the line segment for $x\in [-1,1),$ and the line segments for $x\in [1,3].$ Therefore, we can write the required integral as follows:

$$
{\int }_{-3}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x={{{\int }_{-3}^{-2}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{1}}+{{{\int }_{-2}^{-1}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{-{A}_{2}}+{{{\int }_{-1}^{1}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{3}}+{{{\int }_{1}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{-{A}_{4}}
$$

- The $1$st integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [-3,-2).$ The corresponding region is a triangle, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{1} & =\frac{1}{2}bh \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 1\cdot 2 \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

- The $2$nd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [-2,-1).$ The corresponding region is a triangle, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{2} & =\frac{1}{2}bh \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 1\cdot 2 \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the region lies below the $x$-axis, we have 

$$
{\int }_{-2}^{-1}f(x)\,\text{d}x=-{A}_{2}=-1.
$$

- The $3$rd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [-1,1).$ The corresponding region is a triangle, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{3} & =\frac{1}{2}bh \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 2\cdot 2 \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

- The $4$th integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [1,3].$ The corresponding region is a triangle, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{4} & =\frac{1}{2}bh \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 2\cdot 2 \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the region lies below the $x$-axis, we have 

$$
{\int }_{1}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x=-{A}_{4}=-2.
$$

Finally, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-3}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x & ={A}_{1}-{A}_{2}+{A}_{3}-{A}_{4} \\  & =1-1+2-2 \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$
{\int }_{-5}^{4}f(x)\,\text{d}x={{{\int }_{-5}^{-4}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{1}}+{{{\int }_{-4}^{-3}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{-{A}_{2}}+{{{\int }_{-3}^{0}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{3}}+{{{\int }_{0}^{4}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{4}}.
$$

- The $1$st integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [-5,-4].$ The corresponding region is a triangle, so

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{1} & =\frac{1}{2}(bh) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(1\cdot 2) \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

- The $2$nd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [-4,-3).$ The corresponding region is a triangle, so

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{2} & =\frac{1}{2}(bh) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(1\cdot 2) \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the region lies below the $x$-axis, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-4}^{-3}f(x)\,\text{d}x & =-{A}_{2}=-1.\end{aligned}
$$

- The $3$rd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [-3,0].$ The corresponding region is a triangle, so

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{3} & =\frac{1}{2}(bh) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(3\cdot 3) \\  & =\frac{9}{2}.\end{aligned}

- The $4$th integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in (0,4].$ The corresponding region is a rectangle, so

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-5}^{4}f(x)\,\text{d}x & ={A}_{1}-{A}_{2}+{A}_{3}+{A}_{4} \\  & =1-1+\frac{9}{2}+4 \\  & =\frac{17}{2}.\end{aligned}

Given the graph of $y=f(x)$ above, find the value of ${\int }_{-4}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x.$
questions.worked_solution:
The graph consists of three parts: the line segment for $x\in [-4,-2],$ the arc of a semi-circle for $x\in (-2,2],$ and the line segment for $x\in (2,3].$  So, we can use the additive property of integrals to get

$$
{\int }_{-4}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x={{{\int }_{-4}^{-2}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{1}}+{{{\int }_{-2}^{2}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{-{A}_{2}}+{{{\int }_{2}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{3}}.
$$

The first integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [-4,-2].$ The corresponding region is a rectangle, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{1} & =bh \\  & =2\cdot 3 \\  & =6.\end{aligned}
$$

The second integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in (-2,2].$ The corresponding region is a semi-circle of radius $2.$ Thus, we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{2} & =\frac{1}{2}(\pi {r}^{2}) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(\pi \cdot {2}^{2}) \\  & =2\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

Since the region lies below the $x$-axis, we have

$$
{\int }_{-2}^{2}f(x)\,\text{d}x=-{A}_{2}=-2\pi .
$$

The third integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in (2,3].$ The corresponding region is a trapezoid. Thus, we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{3} & =\frac{1}{2}(a+b)h \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(2+4)(1) \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-4}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x & ={A}_{1}-{A}_{2}+{A}_{3} \\  & =6-2\pi +3 \\  & =9-2\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

$$
{\int }_{-3}^{7}f(x)\,\text{d}x={{{\int }_{-3}^{-1}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{-{A}_{1}}+{{{\int }_{-1}^{1}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{-{A}_{2}}+{{{\int }_{1}^{4}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{3}}+{{{\int }_{4}^{7}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{4}}.
$$

- The $1$st integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [-3,-1].$ The corresponding region is a combination of a rectangle and a quarter-circle of radius $2,$ so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{1} & =bh-\frac{1}{4}\pi {r}^{2} \\  & =(2)(3)-\frac{1}{4}\pi (2)^{2} \\  & =6-\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

Since the region lies below the $x$-axis, we have

$$
{\int }_{-3}^{-1}f(x)\,\text{d}x=-{A}_{1}=\pi -6.
$$

- The $2$nd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [-1,1].$ The corresponding region is a rectangle, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{2} & =bh \\  & =2\cdot 1 \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the region lies below the $x$-axis, we have

$$
{\int }_{-1}^{1}f(x)\,\text{d}x=-{A}_{2}=-2.
$$

- The $3$rd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in (1,4].$ The corresponding region is a trapezoid, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{3} & =\frac{1}{2}(a+b)h \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(1+3)\cdot 3 \\  & =6.\end{aligned}
$$

- The $4$th integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [4,7].$ The corresponding region is a quarter-circle of radius $3,$ so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{4} & =\frac{1}{4}\pi {r}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\pi (3)^{2} \\  & =\frac{9\pi }{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-3}^{7}f(x)\,\text{d}x & =-{A}_{1}-{A}_{2}+{A}_{3}+{A}_{4} \\  & =\pi -6-2+6+\frac{9\pi }{4} \\  & =-2+\frac{13\pi }{4} \\  & =\frac{13\pi -8}{4}.\end{aligned}

- The $1$st integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [-4,0).$ The corresponding region is a semi-circle, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{1} & =\frac{1}{2}\pi {r}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\pi \cdot (2)^{2} \\  & =2\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

- The $2$nd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [0,4].$ The corresponding region is a triangle, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{2} & =\frac{1}{2}b\cdot h \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 4\cdot 4 \\  & =8.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-4}^{4}f(x)\,\text{d}x & ={A}_{1}+{A}_{2} \\  & =2\pi +8.\end{aligned}
$$

The graph of $y=f(x),$ shown above, consists of two line segments. Find the value of $\displaystyle \int_{0}^{4} f(x)\: \textrm{d}x.$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
The graph consists of two parts: the line segment for $x \in [0,2)$ and the line segment for $x \in [2,4].$ Therefore, we can write the required integral as follows:

$$
\int_{0}^{4} f(x)\: \textrm{d}x = \underbrace{\int_{0}^{2} f(x)\: \textrm{d}x}_{A_1} + \underbrace{\int_{2}^{4} f(x)\: \textrm{d}x}_{-A_2}.
$$

- The $1$st integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x \in [0,2).$ The corresponding region is a rectangle, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{1} & =bh \\  & =2\cdot 2 \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

- The $2$nd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x \in [2,4].$ The corresponding region is a right triangle, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{2} & =\frac{1}{2}bh \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 2\cdot 2 \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the region lies below the $x$-axis, we have 

$$
\int_{2}^{4} f(x)\: \textrm{d}x =-A_2 = -2.
$$

Finally, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{4}f(x)\,\text{d}x & ={A}_{1}-{A}_{2} \\  & =4-2 \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Given the graph of $y=f(x)$ above, find the value of $\displaystyle \int_{-4}^4 f(x) \,\textrm{d}x.$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
The graph consists of four parts: the arc of a semi-circle for $x\in [-4,0],$ a line segment for $x\in (0,2),$ a line segment for $x\in (2,4],$ and the point at $x=2.$ So, we can use the additive property of integrals to get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-4}^{4}f(x)\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{-4}^{0}f(x)\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{0}^{2}f(x)\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{2}^{2}f(x)\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{2}^{4}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={{{\int }_{-4}^{0}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{1}}+{{{\int }_{0}^{2}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{-{A}_{2}}+0+{{{\int }_{2}^{4}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{3}}.\end{aligned}
$$

- The $1$st integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x \in [-4,0].$ The corresponding region is a semi-circle with a radius of $2,$ so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{1} & =\frac{1}{2}\pi {r}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot \pi \cdot {2}^{2} \\  & =2\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

- The $2$nd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x \in (0,2).$ The corresponding region is a right triangle, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{2} & =\frac{1}{2}bh \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 2\cdot 2 \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the region lies below the $x$-axis, we have

$$
\int_{0}^{2} f(x)\: \textrm{d}x = -A_2 = -2.
$$

- The $3$rd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x \in (2,4].$  The corresponding region is a right triangle, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{3} & =\frac{1}{2}bh \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 2\cdot 2 \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-4}^{4}f(x)\,\text{d}x & ={A}_{1}-{A}_{2}+{A}_{3} \\  & =2\pi -2+2 \\  & =2\pi .\end{aligned}
$$
